questions.q: Which connective tissue sheath surrounds an individual bundle (fascicle) of skeletal muscle fibers?
questions.explain: Epimysium surrounds the entire muscle belly, perimysium wraps each fascicle of muscle fibers, and endomysium (a delicate reticular fiber layer and external lamina) invests each individual muscle fiber.

open.q: Name the connective tissue layer that envelops a single fascicle of skeletal muscle fibers.

questions.q: Where are the multiple nuclei of a mature skeletal muscle fiber located?
options: At the periphery of the fiber immediately beneath the sarcolemma
In the center of the fiber surrounded by a perinuclear halo
Inside the terminal cisternae of the sarcoplasmic reticulum
Within the Z-disc of each sarcomere
questions.explain: Mature skeletal muscle fibers are multinucleated syncytia formed by the fusion of myoblasts, with elongated nuclei pushed to the periphery just beneath the sarcolemma.

open.q: Describe the characteristic intracellular location of the nuclei in a mature skeletal muscle fiber.
accept: at the periphery of the cell

questions.q: Which stem cells reside between the sarcolemma and the external (basal) lamina of skeletal muscle fibers and proliferate to regenerate damaged muscle after injury?
questions.explain: Satellite cells are quiescent, mononucleated myogenic stem cells situated inside the external lamina of adult skeletal muscle fibers that activate, divide, and fuse to repair focal muscle injury.

open.q: Name the quiescent myogenic stem cells located between the sarcolemma and basal lamina of skeletal muscle fibers that mediate muscle regeneration.

questions.q: What defines the structural boundaries of a single sarcomere, the functional contractile unit of striated muscle?
options: The borders of a single A-band
questions.explain: A sarcomere extends from one Z-disc to the next Z-disc, encompassing one central A-band and two adjacent half I-bands.

open.q: Between which two transverse protein structures is a single sarcomere bounded?

questions.q: Which protein forms the major structural component of the Z-disc and anchors the barbed (+) ends of thin actin filaments?
questions.explain: Alpha-actinin cross-links antiparallel actin thin filaments at the Z-disc, whereas myomesin cross-links thick myosin filaments at the M-line.

open.q: Name the actin-binding protein in the Z-disc that anchors the thin filaments of adjacent sarcomeres.

questions.q: During skeletal muscle contraction, which bands or zones of the sarcomere shorten while the A-band remains constant in width?
options: Both the I-band and the H-zone shorten
The A-band widens while the I-band remains unchanged
The Z-discs lengthen while the H-zone widens
questions.explain: Because thick (myosin) and thin (actin) filaments slide past each other without changing length, the anisotropic A-band stays constant in width while the I-band (thin filaments only) and H-zone (thick filaments only) narrow.

open.q: Which two regions of the sarcomere decrease in width during muscle contraction while the A-band stays constant?

questions.q: Which giant elastic protein extends from the Z-disc to the M-line, centering the thick myosin filaments within the sarcomere and providing passive elasticity?
questions.explain: Titin is the largest known human protein; it spans half a sarcomere from the Z-disc to the M-line, keeping myosin thick filaments centered and acting as a molecular spring.

open.q: Name the giant elastic sarcomeric protein that anchors thick filaments to the Z-disc and prevents overstretching of the sarcomere.

questions.q: Which regulatory protein subunit binds calcium ions released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum to initiate cross-bridge cycling in striated muscle?
questions.explain: Troponin C binds four calcium ions, inducing a conformational change that pulls tropomyosin away from the myosin-binding sites on F-actin; smooth muscle lacks troponin and uses calmodulin instead.

open.q: Which specific subunit of the troponin complex binds calcium ions in skeletal and cardiac muscle?

questions.q: In mammalian skeletal muscle, where are the transverse tubules (T-tubules) and flanking terminal cisternae of the sarcoplasmic reticulum (triads) located relative to the sarcomere?
options: At the A-I band junctions (two triads per sarcomere)
At the Z-discs (one triad per sarcomere)
At the M-line in the center of the A-band
Outside the external lamina in the endomysium
questions.explain: In skeletal muscle, T-tubules invaginate at the junction between the A-band and I-band and are flanked on both sides by terminal cisternae to form triads (two per sarcomere). In cardiac muscle, diads occur at the Z-disc.

open.q: At which sarcomeric landmark are T-tubule triads located in mammalian skeletal muscle fibers?
accept: junction of A and I bands

questions.q: Which calcium release channel on the terminal cisternae of the sarcoplasmic reticulum opens in response to depolarization of the T-tubule dihydropyridine (DHP) receptor?
questions.explain: In skeletal muscle, voltage-sensing dihydropyridine (DHP) receptors in the T-tubule membrane mechanically couple to ryanodine receptor-1 (RyR1) channels on the sarcoplasmic reticulum, releasing stored calcium into the sarcoplasm.

open.q: Name the sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium-release channel coupled to the T-tubule dihydropyridine receptor.

questions.q: A 5-year-old boy presents with progressive proximal muscle weakness, calf pseudohypertrophy, and Gowers sign (Duchenne muscular dystrophy). Which subsarcolemmal protein linking intracellular actin filaments to the extracellular matrix via beta-dystroglycan is absent?
questions.explain: Dystrophin links the internal F-actin cytoskeleton to the transmembrane dystrophin-associated glycoprotein complex (dystroglycans/sarcoglycans) and laminin; its absence causes sarcolemmal tearing during contraction and myofiber necrosis.

open.q: Mutation and loss of which subsarcolemmal cytoskeletal linker protein causes Duchenne muscular dystrophy?

questions.q: Which histological and metabolic features characterize Type I (slow oxidative / red) skeletal muscle fibers?
options: Abundant mitochondria, high myoglobin content, rich capillary supply, and fatigue resistance
Low myoglobin, few mitochondria, abundant glycogen, and rapid fatigue
Complete absence of striations and voluntary control
Multiple central nuclei with intercalated discs
questions.explain: Type I slow oxidative fibers appear dark red due to rich myoglobin and capillary density, contain numerous mitochondria for aerobic ATP production, and sustain prolonged postural contractions without fatigue.

open.q: Which oxygen-binding heme protein gives Type I slow oxidative skeletal muscle fibers their characteristic red color?

questions.q: Which specialized end-to-end junctional complexes join adjacent cardiac muscle cells and contain fascia adherens, desmosomes, and gap junctions?
questions.explain: Intercalated discs are step-like transverse/lateral junctions at the Z-disc level between cardiomyocytes; their transverse portions contain fascia adherens and desmosomes for mechanical force transmission, while their longitudinal portions contain gap junctions for rapid electrical coupling.

open.q: Name the specialized step-like intercellular junctional complexes that electrically and mechanically couple adjacent cardiomyocytes.

questions.q: Which component of the lateral (longitudinal) portion of an intercalated disc allows action potentials to spread rapidly from one cardiomyocyte to the next so the myocardium contracts as a functional syncytium?
questions.explain: Gap junctions (connexon channels) lie along the longitudinal steps of the intercalated disc parallel to the myofibrils, permitting low-resistance ionic current flow between adjacent cardiac cells.

open.q: Which intercellular junction located in the longitudinal segment of the intercalated disc enables direct ionic current spread between cardiomyocytes?

questions.q: Which endocrine peptide hormone is stored in membrane-bound granules near the nuclei of right atrial cardiomyocytes and secreted in response to atrial stretch?
questions.explain: Atrial myocytes contain juxtanuclear electron-dense granules storing atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP), which promotes renal sodium and water excretion and vasodilation when atrial pressure rises.

open.q: Name the natriuretic hormone synthesized and stored in perinuclear granules of atrial cardiac muscle cells.

questions.q: How do Purkinje fibers of the cardiac conducting system differ histologically from ordinary working ventricular cardiomyocytes?
options: They are larger, stain paler due to abundant glycogen, and have fewer peripherally displaced myofibrils
They are smaller, multinucleated, and lack gap junctions
They are unstriated spindle-shaped cells innervated by somatic motor neurons
They contain dense bodies instead of Z-discs
questions.explain: Subendocardial Purkinje fibers are modified cardiomyocytes specialized for rapid impulse conduction; they have a wider diameter, prominent perinuclear glycogen-rich pale cytoplasm, sparse peripheral myofibrils, and abundant gap junctions.

open.q: Which cytoplasmic storage carbohydrate accumulates abundantly in cardiac Purkinje fibers, giving them a pale appearance on H&E staining?

questions.q: Which electron-dense cytoplasmic and subsarcolemmal structures in smooth muscle cells serve as the functional equivalent of Z-discs by anchoring thin actin filaments and desmin intermediate filaments?
questions.explain: Smooth muscle lacks sarcomeres and Z-discs; instead, alpha-actinin-rich dense bodies in the cytoplasm and attachment plaques on the sarcolemma anchor thin actin filaments and intermediate filaments (desmin/vimentin).

open.q: Name the alpha-actinin-containing structures in smooth muscle cells that anchor actin thin filaments and intermediate filaments in place of Z-discs.

questions.q: In smooth muscle contraction, calcium ions bind to calmodulin and activate which enzyme to phosphorylate myosin regulatory light chains?
questions.explain: Because smooth muscle lacks troponin, intracellular calcium binds calmodulin; the Ca2+-calmodulin complex activates myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK), which phosphorylates myosin light chains to enable actin-myosin cross-bridging.

open.q: Which enzyme activated by the calcium-calmodulin complex phosphorylates myosin light chains to trigger smooth muscle contraction?

questions.q: Which small flask-shaped plasma membrane invaginations in smooth muscle cells substitute for T-tubules by sequestering calcium and triggering calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum?
questions.explain: Smooth muscle cells lack T-tubules and instead possess numerous subsarcolemmal vesicular invaginations called caveolae that concentrate calcium channels near cortical sarcoplasmic reticulum.

open.q: Name the flask-shaped sarcolemmal invaginations in smooth muscle cells that function analogously to T-tubules in calcium signaling.

questions.q: Which encapsulated stretch-receptor organ lies in parallel with extrafusal skeletal muscle fibers and contains nuclear bag and nuclear chain intrafusal fibers?
questions.explain: Muscle spindles are fusiform encapsulated proprioceptors embedded parallel to extrafusal muscle fibers; they monitor changes in muscle length and velocity via nuclear bag and nuclear chain intrafusal fibers innervated by gamma motor neurons and Ia/II sensory afferents.

open.q: Name the encapsulated proprioceptive stretch receptor within skeletal muscle belly that contains nuclear bag and nuclear chain intrafusal fibers.
